upstream.note: repo/commit above are the mirror this build checks out. It is a verbatim copy of the upstream tree at mirror_of_commit, minus stock/ (see the mirror's NOTICE.md). Using the mirror keeps the build working if upstream collects the commit objects of the branch it since deleted.
upstream.note_updater: mu300-update is not taken from the upstream release: that file (sha256 99e32cb6...) is older than the pinned tree's own updater (it still writes boot_b only, without the Linux slot detection), and devices replace their updater with the release's one before they update. The build publishes the tree's rootfs/overlay/opt/mu300/bin/mu300-update with scripts/local-adaptations.patch applied - the same file the rootfs carries, and what upstream's own tools/make-release.sh publishes.

kernels.stable_note: stable_series is the default mainline kernel of every device (mu300-kernel-7.2.tar.gz); extra_series are built and published next to it (mu300-kernel-7.3.tar.gz) for devices that ask for them by name: 'mu300-update kernel 7.3'. Each is the newest point release of its series from kernel.org's sha256sums.asc, which also lists the releases of an end-of-life series (7.2). Nothing moves a device to another series by itself: the updater (scripts/local-adaptations.patch) knows KERNELS="5.4 6.18 7.2 7.3" and installs the bundle of the device's own choice. A manual run can override the versions (kv_stable, kv_extra).
kernels.note: no digest is pinned here: kernel.org's own sha256sums.asc is the source of truth, so a new point release needs no change
